title: Blue Star Museums
description: As part of the Blue Star Museums program, the San Diego Archaeological Center offers free admission to active-duty military personnel and their families from Armed Forces Day through Labor Day. The military ID holder can be either active duty service member or other dependent family member with the appropriate ID card. The active duty member does not have to be present for family members to use the program. Just bring your DD Form 1173 ID Card, or DD Form 1173-1 ID Card, for active duty military family members. About Blue Star Museums: Blue Star Museums is a collaboration among the National Endowment for the Arts, Blue Star Families, the Department of War, and museums across America to offer free admission to the nation’s active duty military personnel including National Guard and Reserve and their families each summer. The program begins on Armed Forces Day in mid-May and ends on Labor Day at the beginning of September. For more information, including a full list of participating museums, visit the Blue Star Families website .

description:

Best of all, get a look at our brand-new exhibition, Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea and grab a drink in the dive bar while chatting with a scientist. We welcome the community to spend a day with us at Rancho Guajome Adobe, tour the adobe, enjoy our gardens, trails and also have an afternoon picnic at our picnic tables. Watch a traditional loom demonstration and learn about the art of weaving.

Join our knowledgeable docent for a guided tour of the historic Rancho Guajome Adobe.

Adults $3.00 (13 and older)

Cash or check only

partner_name: San Diego County Parks and Recreation
description:
Looking for something fun to do with the family? Pack up the kids and head to San Elijo Lagoon Nature Center for nature-themed crafts and activities, including our TRACK Trail program. The whole family will enjoy exploring Nature Center exhibits, the surrounding grounds and loop trail. Plan ahead and enjoy a picnic on the upstairs observation deck! Sunday Family Funday is a free event in which a different aspect of nature is explored each month.

Family Fun Day Topic: Bugs!

Inclement weather may cancel; call ahead.
Phone: (760) 634-3026
location: San Elijo Lagoon Ecological Reserve, 2710 Manchester Ave, Cardiff, CA 92007, USA

title: Guided Nature Walk from the Visitor Center
description:
Join an MTRP Trail Guide on a special Martin Luther King Day nature walk and learn about the plants, animals, geology, history, and ecology of the park on one of these scenic trails:

  *   The Oak Grove Loop showcasing majestic coast live oaks and rare Engelmann’s oaks.
  *   The Visitor Center Loop highlighting coastal sage scrub, chaparral, and riparian woodland habitats.
  *   The Riverside Grinding Rocks featuring one of the archaeological sites in the park.

These interpretive nature walks are offered to enhance your appreciation of the unique beauty of San Diego’s natural environment.  The park is constantly changing, so see and learn new things on walks throughout the year.
Walks start from the Visitor Center every Saturday, Sunday, and Wednesday at 9:30 a.m.  Walks are free and open to the public, with no reservations required.
The trails used are easy, but have uneven surfaces and some involve steps, so be sure to wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes and bring along water.  A hat and sunscreen are also recommended.  Walks are canceled if raining.
location: Mission Trails Regional Park Visitor Center (1 Father Junipero Serra Trl, San Diego, CA 92119, United States)

title: Senior Monday
description: Come join us for an engaging lecture on fascinating scientific topics, followed by an unforgettable show in the Heikoff Giant Dome Theater—all for the discounted admission of $10! It's a great way to learn something new and connect with others in our community. Plus, enjoy engaging and interactive experiences that you won't want to miss. We can't wait to explore the wonders of science with you! Click here to see the lineup of lecture topics, speakers and documentaries. Tickets are available only at the ticket counter on the day of the event. Fleet Members have free access to the Sharp Minds lecture.

description: Be an Ocean Connector and start your day with birding and brews! Sip on smooth, nitro cold brew from Trident Coffee as you learn how their values of connection, community, and character align with our conservation mission. Then, head out on a guided walking tour along the Bayshore Bikeway at South San Diego Bay, equipped with binoculars and field guides. What to Expect: Coffee Tasting: Kick off the tour with a unique nitro cold brew tasting, crafted locally by Trident Coffee. Birdwatching Walk: Explore the Bayshore Bikeway with expert guides to spot native and migratory birds. Ecology & Conservation: Learn about local ecosystems and conservation efforts to protect our coastal wildlife. Best of all, every tour supports our education programs for South Bay youth!

title: Project NexTech: Natural Sciences Workshop
description: On alternating Tuesdays, we'll have Project NexTech teaching basic engineering and natural science in a fun way! title: Teen Service Learning Orientation
description: Do you need hours for high school requirements, college applications, scholarships, or work experience? Then consider interviewing to be a Teen Service Learner at the Vista Library. Pickup an application at the library, fill it out, and show up to be informally interviewed alongside your peers. Interview will cover the requirements, duties/responsibilities, and opportunities offered by the Vista Library’s Teen Service Learner program. The Teen Service Learner Program is open to teens ages 13-17 and requires a minimum 40-hour service commitment from each participant. For more details please contact the Teen Service Learner Coordinator Daniel Aguilar at vistalibrary@sdcounty.ca.gov or call 760-643-5100.

description:

title: Fizz & Ferment: The Art of Kombucha
description:
Fizz, flavor, and a little fermentation magic! Join UC Master Food Preservers for a 90-minute class all about crafting your own fermented beverages at home. You’ll learn the basics of fermentation and dive into the art of making kombucha—from brewing your first batch to safely fermenting and flavoring it with fruits, herbs, and spices.

This hands-on workshop will guide you through each step, with plenty of tips to help you create delicious, bubbly kombucha tailored to your taste. Each participant will take home a starter kit to make their first batch at home with confidence.

This free class will be held at the Oceanside Public Library Mission Branch. Registration is required.

Come ready to sip, learn, and get brewing!

description: Join Project Wildlife for a brown-bag lunch info session with their amazing animal ambassadors! Raptors are found in all kinds of habitats on land — provided there is enough food! Bring a lunch and a friend and learn all about Raptors and the their critical role in our ecosystem.

title: Knot Together
description: Inspired by the traditional fishing nets and nautical knots featured in To Catch a Fish , our newest Together workshop series, Knot Together , explores the art of macramé. The series is led by Sitoë Thiam, a fiber artist and mechanical engineer who bridges technical precision with organic expression. As the founder of Unknot, a design studio specializing in knotting and weaving, she brings a unique interdisciplinary perspective to the world of fiber arts. Knotted Rope Wall Hanging In September, learn to transform rope into a sculptural wall hanging. You’ll explore four foundational knots, building a rhythmic, colorful composition that celebrates the tactile beauty of fiber. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , and Clay Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.

title: Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour
description: Be an Ocean Connector and join us for a Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour! Join us for a guided Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour through the beautiful waterways of South San Diego Bay, ending in the restored Chula Vista Wetlands. This scenic, two-hour paddle offers a unique opportunity to explore coastal habitats while learning about the wildlife and conservation efforts that make South San Diego Bay so special. Along the way, you may spot osprey diving for fish, great blue herons and egrets wading in the shallows, nesting terns (April to September), and a variety of migrating birds (October to March). With a little luck, guests can even catch a glimpse of a Pacific green sea turtle cruising through the bay! This tour is welcoming to all skill levels and moves at a comfortable pace, with plenty of time to enjoy the surroundings. The route is about two hours long, and wind conditions can vary, adding a bit of adventure while still remaining accessible for beginners. description: Join San Diego Bird Alliance and our partners for a fun, free, family-friendly morning celebrating the incredible biodiversity of Mission Bay's wetlands! San Diego Coastkeeper will lead a bilingual (English-Spanish) Water Quality Demonstration and provide insight into our latest 2025 Mission Bay Water Quality Report. This bilingual (English/Spanish) community event offers opportunities to connect with nature while contributing to community science during California Biodiversity Day. Activities include: Bird watching walk Fish seining demonstration Invertebrate exploration Native plant walk Nature observations with iNaturalist Water quality talk and demonstration Educational activities for all ages Whether you're an experienced naturalist or visiting the wetlands for the first time, everyone is welcome! Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026 Time: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM Location: UC San Diego Kendall-Frost Marsh (Crown Point Entrance) Come discover the amazing wildlife of Mission Bay and celebrate Latino Conservation Week and California Biodiversity Day with us! For questions, contact: Kornelas@sandiegobirdalliance.org Bring: Weather-appropriate attire and water Optional: Waterproof shoes and a camera We will meet at the southern end of Crown Point Park, near the dirt lot. Parking: San Diego, CA 92109 Address: Crown Point Dr, San Diego, CA 92109 Coordinates: 32°47'21.2″N 117°13'54.8″W Google Maps Link Register Here! Important Notes: Age: This event is suitable for all ages, though children must be accompanied by an adult. Accessibility: Please be aware that the terrain will include uneven sandy beaches. Expect to travel a short distance from the parking area to the meeting point and navigate uneven terrain, so be prepared for a bit of a trek. Weather Reminder: The event will take place rain or shine, but please check for updates in case of severe weather conditions. Safety: Please stay within the designated areas and respect the natural environment. Why Fish Seining? Fish play a critical role in maintaining the food web; they are an essential food source for many bird species. By monitoring fish populations through activities like fish seining, we can gain insight into the health of the marsh’s aquatic habitats. Healthy fish populations indicate clean, thriving waters, which ultimately benefit the birds that call the marsh home. In essence, by protecting the fish, we are also protecting the birds and the broader ecosystem. So, when you help us with fish seining, you’re not just learning about fish—you’re contributing to the long-term conservation of both the birds and the habitat they rely on. This is a partnership project between UC San Diego Natural Reserve System and San Diego Bird Alliance.

Participants can explore the wetlands through bilingual guided walks, birdwatching, nature talks, hands-on activities, arts and crafts, and interactive science experiences. One of the highlights will be a hands-on experience in the estuary, where participants can help plant 50 native plants, take part in a water quality demonstration, and spend time with biologists. Local conservation experts will help participants understand what these activities reveal about the health and importance of our wetlands. Families can also explore local biodiversity using iNaturalist, connect with conservation organizations, and discover nature up close through specimens, microscopes, field guides, and other educational tools. Latino Conservation Week is more than a celebration of nature. It is a celebration of community, culture, and collective action. title: Community Science Plastic Pellet (Nurdle) Cleanup 9/19/26
description: Join us at Rotary Park in Carlsbad for a community science plastic pellet (nurdle) cleanup. Plastic pellets are the building blocks of the plastic supply chain, making so many of the products we use in our daily lives — everything from milk jugs to plastic bags. Unfortunately, they are also entering our environment at staggering rates, with more than 10 trillion plastic pellets entering our oceans annually. We are planning to continually monitor this site and collect data to address and quantify plastic pellet pollution in our communities and treasured waterways. The California coast has seen plastic pellet pollution in recent years, and the data collected through pellet counts paves the way for lasting change. title: The Flight of Jackie Cochran Documentary Screening
description: Documentary Screening at the San Diego Air & Space Museum Friday, September 25, 2026 1:00 p.m. Pavilion of Flight Discover the remarkable story of one of aviation’s most accomplished—and often overlooked—pioneers during a special screening of The Flight of Jackie Cochran at the San Diego Air & Space Museum. The documentary will be presented on the Museum’s state-of-the-art LED video wall in the Pavilion of Flight. About the Documentary The Flight of Jackie Cochran tells the story of “the most famous pilot you’ve never heard of”—a woman who shattered aviation records, broke the sound barrier and helped change the course of history, only to be largely forgotten by it. A contemporary and rival of Amelia Earhart, Jackie Cochran became one of the most influential figures in American aviation. During World War II, she played a central role in establishing the Women Airforce Service Pilots, better known as the WASP, and later set an extraordinary number of speed, distance and altitude records. Behind Cochran’s public achievements, however, was a private life carefully constructed to conceal her past. Drawing on newly discovered archival materials and personal correspondence, the documentary explores a long-buried secret from her childhood and examines how her beginnings shaped her ambition, determination and relentless drive to succeed. The film also features scenes from the stage play The Flight of Jackie Cochran , written by and starring Nancy Hasty. Based on archival material uncovered during Hasty’s research, these dramatic reenactments bring Cochran’s voice and inner world to life while connecting her personal struggles with her historic accomplishments. More than a traditional biography, The Flight of Jackie Cochran examines how history chooses its heroes and why some extraordinary stories fade from public memory. It is a powerful exploration of ambition, perseverance, identity and the cost of greatness. Admission The screening is included with general Museum admission and is free for: San Diego Air & Space Museum Members Balboa Park Explorer Pass holders Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

description: Speakers: Ulrike Arnold , Artist; Gerard van Belle, PhD , Former Director of Science at Lowell Observatory; and Rachel Jans, PhD , Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at The San Diego Museum of Art MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater   Meteorites as Artistic Matter brings together internationally acclaimed artist Ulrike Arnold, astronomer Gerard van Belle, and the Museum’s Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art Rachel Jans, PhD, for a fascinating interdisciplinary conversation exploring the intersection of art, science, and the cosmos. Known for incorporating meteorite dust and pigments gathered from some of the world’s most remote landscapes into her paintings, Arnold will discuss how celestial and earthly materials become powerful artistic media. Joined by van Belle’s astronomical perspective and Jans’s expertise on the work of Sigmar Polke, a German artist also known for incorporating unconventional materials into his work, and contemporary artistic practice, this engaging guest lecture offers a rare opportunity to discover how meteorites inspire creativity, expand our understanding of materiality, and connect artistic expression with the vast universe beyond our planet. Following the lecture, guests are invited to enjoy a guided tour led by our docent team.   Please note, this lecture is in-person only and held at the MOPA@SDMA Joan and Irwin Jacobs Theater in Balboa Park. $15 members and students | $20 seniors and military | $30 nonmembers This lecture is presented as a part of the Guest Lecture Series , which offers a platform for renowned scholars and experts from the art world to share their insights and knowledge on topics related to art history, art theory, and the museum’s collections.

What to Expect:   Approximately 7 miles of moderate hiking with ~1,200 ft elevation gain, some uneven terrain, off-trail sections and light scrambling    Dramatic badlands, natural arches, and sculpted sandstone domes    Panoramic views of the Carrizo Badlands and Imperial Valley    A chance to see desert wildlife and seasonal blooms    Interpretive insights into the area’s unique geology and desert ecology   Who Should Attend:   Hikers with some experience looking for a moderate challenge    Nature and geology enthusiasts eager to explore off-the-beaten-path areas    Visitors eager to experience one of Anza-Borrego’s most fascinating natural features     REGISTER TODAY! Cost:  ABF Member: $30  Non-Member: $35  Student: $18    Cancellation Policy & Scholarships: Please see our FAQs page to read our cancellation policy and learn about scholarship options.  What Previous Attendees Are Saying about Our Hikes:  “I loved the hike choice and challenge. I will definitely be on another hike with the foundation soon!”  “I so enjoyed getting "off trail" and exploring with the Anza Borrego Foundation. The camaraderie, physical challenge, and education around Anza Borrego was beyond my expectations.”  “Expertise was great. cohesiveness of group was good. location excellent.”  Hike Leader:  In his professional life, Sergey Kuhsch has spent over 16 years in software development across different industries. In contrast, much of his free time is dedicated to exploring the natural world. As much as he enjoys hiking in chaparral or exploring the local mountains, he feels that Anza Borrego is a very special place. The sheer size and accessibility of the park are unlike any other in the region. The rugged landscape, endless vistas, and hidden oases offer unique opportunities to explore. Sergey feels that supporting the Anza Borrego Foundation is the most impactful way to support Anza Borrego Desert State Park.                                              You’re invited to explore the scientific detective story in San Diego’s diverse mountains and deserts spanning over 200 million years.  This includes the expansive landscapes of Anza-Borrego Desert State Park which is rich with ancient geological wonders.

title: Skate Craft: Do-It-Yourself Design in Skateboarding
description: Celebrate skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, from the boards, gear, and ramps, to the machines and the repurposed boards as objects of use. To land a trick, to make the make—that moment is everything. It’s the struggle between you and the skateboard, the challenge of turning something sketchy into a clean run. Whether it's mastering a carve, dropping in, or landing a trick, the average number of attempts is 10,000. When you finally achieve it, that's when it becomes a true "MAKE." This exhibition celebrates skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, tracing its evolution from the early days of making decks in garages and building ramps from found lumber to the handcrafted works of art seen today. Experience how skateboarding nurtures creativity, self-expression, and joy through artisanal craftsmanship. The progression of skateboard design, safety gear, and skate shoes, alongside the inventive machines that facilitated their creation, is driven by a DIY ethos. Around the world, artists embrace this spirit by turning old skateboards into jewelry and furniture, demonstrating how skateboarding combines play, design, and sustainability in vibrant ways.
